marks.gloss_en: אין, והתנן ... במנה בן ארבעים סלעים -- a tanna does speak of a maneh of forty sela
and does a tanna teach 'a maneh of forty sela'?
אין! והתנן ... רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר: ... במנה בן ארבעים סלעים (= p_rebey_pakiot_shel_shti)
a new flask, even though it holds pomegranates, is pure
if he sewed it and it tore, its measure is like letting pomegranates out
מנהני מילי? אמר קרא לעמד לשרת -- a thing fit for service
the mishna: [one gives] enough to make a small garment
הוא ובניו -- a thing equal for Aaron and his sons, which the cap is not
אמר קרא הוא ובניו -- a thing equal for Aaron and his sons (= p_hu_uvanav)
the verse says 'he and his sons' (Deut 18:5) -- a thing equal for Aaron and his sons
אימא מעיל! -- say [the garment is] the robe
תפשת מרובה לא תפשת, תפשת מועט תפשת -- if you grasped much you did not grasp; if you grasped little you grasped
ואימא כיפה של צמר, דתניא: a woolen cap was on the High Priest's head beneath the frontplate
a cap of wool was placed on the High Priest's head and the frontplate set upon it, to fulfil what is said 'and you shall put it on a thread of blue' (Ex 28:37)
אבנט נמי לא שוי! -- by the criterion of 'he and his sons' the belt too is not equal; הניחא למאן דאמר לא זהו אבנטו של כהן הדיוט, אלא למאן דאמר זהו, מאי איכא למימר?
the High Priest's belt is the ordinary priest's belt
שם אבנט בעולם -- the name 'belt' exists [for all priests]
he sheared and sold the first -- Rav Chisda: obligated
since the mishna exempts one who bought the gentile's shearing, one who bought the gentile's flock to shear it is obligated
אמאי? כל חד וחד בתר גיזה נפקא לה מרשותיה -- why is he obligated? each one, after its shearing, leaves his possession
we learned: one who buys the shearing of a gentile's flock is exempt from the first shearing
כגון שהקנן לו כל שלשים יום -- where [the gentile] transferred them to him for all thirty days (= p_okimta_hiknan_shloshim)
Rav Chisda interpreted it according to R' Natan bar Hoshaya: where he transferred them to him for all thirty days
Rav Chisda: one who sheared and sold [each in turn] is obligated [in the first shearing]
the mishna: how much does one give him? [the weight of five sela,] laundered and not soiled
דתנן: המוכר קלחי אילן... אמר רבי יהודה: ...שייר בעל השדה -- נותן פאה על הכל (bare citation formula; no support kind of its own)
Rav Chisda: it is R' Yehuda
דתנן: מכור לי בני מעיה של פרה זו... (bare citation formula; no support kind of its own)
rather, Rava: it is this tanna [of the innards mishna]
והא מר הוא דאמר: והוא שהתחיל בעל השדה לקצור -- by your own word R' Yehuda's ruling needs the owner to have begun harvesting (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)
Rav Chisda's own statement, cited by Rava: and that is when the field-owner began to harvest
בשלמא התם ובקצרכם כתיב... אלא הכא מעידנא דאתחיל למיגז לא מיחייב בכוליה עדריה
and if you say: here too, [the seller is obligated] when he began to shear

the mishna: one who buys the shearing of his fellow's flock -- [if the seller kept some, the seller is obligated]; who is the tanna for whom, where there is residue with the seller, we go after the seller?
R' Yehuda: when? when the field-owner did not keep [any]
